observations: A standing figure with arms spread wide occupies the center; layered black, red, and pink lines build the torso and limbs over a muted olive-green ground.
A wide ruffled skirt shape fans out from the waist, formed by radiating white and red lines that splay outward, with loose black scribbles along the hem.
Soft amber-brown shadow shapes sit behind the figure's head, torso, and feet, giving a faint sense of depth against the flat background.
reading: Tangled red and black lines stack into a figure that reads as both skeletal and costumed—the ribbed torso exposed while a radiating skirt asserts ceremony. The spread arms and upright stance carry a sense of display, though the scribbled, unresolved lines keep that reading unstable. Pink and white strokes glow inside the darker mesh, pulling the eye inward toward the chest.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #16 and nnxyz nnotb #18. All three show a full-body figure on a flat ground, but #17 replaces #16's angular yellow grid lines and #18's blue-orange palette with a tighter red-pink-black layering.

connections.reason: Both place a frontal figure with spread arms on an olive ground, but #16 extends rectangular yellow and red grid lines into empty space while #17 keeps all line activity close to the body.
Both figures carry a ruffled skirt-like form at the waist, but #18 renders it in warm orange on teal with an off-balance pose, while #17 holds a symmetrical upright stance in red and pink.

lookingQuestion: Where do the white lines sit relative to the red and black ones, and what does that layering do to the sense of depth in the torso?
ambiguities: The scribbled head area is dense enough that specific facial features cannot be confirmed from the image.
